finding.claim: POP3 retriever disables TLS certificate verification when enable_ssl is set, so the username and password are sent over a connection an on-path attacker can impersonate the server on.
finding.source: Network position between the application and the POP3 server (on-path MITM, hostile DNS or Wi-Fi). Precondition: retriever_method :pop3 with :enable_ssl => true.
finding.sink: pop3.start(settings[:user_name], settings[:password]) at pop3.rb:133, which sends credentials over the TLS session with no peer verification. Retrieved mail is also handed to the app via Mail.new at pop3.rb:76/84.

trace.note: pop3.start sends USER/PASS over the unverified TLS session
Attacker-served mail is parsed with Mail.new and yielded to the app

finding.guards_checked: Only the enable_ssl truthiness check. No verify-mode setting exists for POP3, unlike SMTP (smtp.rb:187-196 honours :openssl_verify_mode and defaults to Net::SMTP's verifying context). IMAP (imap.rb:170) passes no custom SSL context, so it inherits net-imap's default verification. I did not confirm the net-imap default in this tree.

finding.claim: Attachment filenames are interpolated into Content-Type and Content-Disposition header strings without escaping. A name containing a double quote can inject extra header parameters that change the filename the recipient sees (e.g. spoofing the extension). A name containing CR/LF may also inject whole headers, though I did not confirm that part.
finding.source: The attachment name: the hash key in attachments[name]=, or the basename from add_file. Precondition: the app builds the name from user-controlled input.
finding.sink: The header strings built at attachments_list.rb:44-46, serialised by ContentDispositionField#encoded (content_disposition_field.rb:35-36) and ParameterHash#encoded (parameter_hash.rb:51).

trace.note: ASCII-only names are returned unchanged by decode_encode (encodings.rb:110-111)
Name is placed raw inside filename="..." in content_type and line 46 in content_disposition
Part.new(hash) stores the raw strings as header fields
ensure_filename_quoted only quotes an unquoted filename= value; it does not escape embedded quotes or CR/LF
dquote escapes only \\ and "; it does not strip CR/LF, so a raw newline survives if the parser kept it

finding.guards_checked: decode_encode (ASCII passthrough, no escaping). ensure_filename_quoted (no escaping). dquote (quote and backslash only, no CR/LF handling). SmtpEnvelope#validate_addr rejects CR/LF but only for envelope addresses, not header values (smtp_envelope.rb:50). No validation of the attachment name anywhere in the path.

finding.claim: Attachment and add_file read any local file path given to them and attach its contents to outgoing mail, so an app that passes a user-controlled path enables arbitrary file read and exfiltration.
finding.source: The path argument: {filename: path} in attachments[]=, add_file(String), or Mail.read(filename). Precondition: the app passes an attacker-influenced path.
finding.sink: File.open(path, 'rb') { |f| f.read } at attachments_list.rb:50, which copies the file into the message body (sent to the recipient or returned by Mail.read). Also message.rb:1769 and mail.rb:169.

trace.note: File.open reads any readable path with no restriction
add_file(String) takes the path and reads it at 1769

finding.guards_checked: No path allow-list, no symlink or traversal checks, no size limit. File.basename is applied only to the attachment name (message.rb:1768), not to the read path. This is likely an API-contract issue rather than a library bug, so severity depends entirely on the calling app.

finding.claim: IMAP find passes :keys straight into UID SEARCH as the raw search string. If an app builds keys from user input, it may be able to inject extra IMAP commands. Unverified: depends on whether net-imap rejects CR/LF in string arguments.
finding.source: The :keys option. Precondition: an app concatenates user-controlled text into a string passed as keys.
finding.sink: imap.uid_search(options[:keys], ...) at imap.rb:79, which writes the search string into the IMAP command stream.

trace.note: Docs say keys may be a raw string holding the entire search string
validate_options defaults keys to 'ALL' but otherwise keeps the caller's value
Raw value handed to uid_search without validation

finding.guards_checked: validate_options (imap.rb:147-160) only sets defaults. No CR/LF or parenthesis check in this repo. Mailbox names go through encode_utf7 (imap.rb:156) but are not otherwise checked. Whether net-imap escapes or rejects CR/LF was not verified because it is an external gem not in this tree.
